correctness.rationale: For any positive normalized p, one merger changes concentration S by 2ab. Its inverse change strictly increases with ab holding merged mass and remainder square sum fixed, and decreases with remainder square sum. AM–GM and Cauchy–Schwarz force two equal merged abundances and n−2 equal untouched abundances. Exact differentiation of their one-variable loss produces a strictly increasing quartic factor with one positive zero, giving global uniqueness and strict boundary inequalities. Quartic scaling proves M_n/(n−2)→3−2sqrt(2); 2ab/(S+2ab)<1/2 is sharp as a supremum. The packaged standard-library verifier independently checks polynomial identities and 59,776 exact positive-rational test profiles, not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The object is the worst-case *reciprocal* Simpson concentration loss under one arbitrary two-taxon aggregation, optimized over all strictly positive profiles in dimension n. Hill introduced the diversity index and discussed simultaneous category changes but does not state this one-pair extremum. Ecological coarsening studies analyze structured data operations, not the all-profile exact maximum. The Herfindahl merger increase 2ab is a known identity, but its optimizing distribution and unique quartic and asymptotic are additional statements. Searches in ecological/taxonomic and concentration/merger aliases, together with comparisons of nearby published diversity claims, did not identify dominating prior coverage. Residual risk: unlocated reciprocal-Herfindahl optimization.
residual_risks: An equivalent global inverse-Herfindahl single-merger optimization may have appeared in economics or diversity-index methodology under different terminology.

value.rationale: Taxonomic consolidation is a natural source of ecological-diversity measurement distortion. The exact sharp n-dependent worst-case loss, its unique optimally imbalanced two-level abundance profile, and a new linear loss coefficient contrast with the bounded two-unit loss for equal abundances. The relative loss is always below half despite unbounded absolute loss. These are operationally interpretable limits for one binning operation, distinct from the trivial change of raw squared concentration.
